# Preparation before class

```{r, include=FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(styler)
library(tidyverse)
library(installr)
library(foreign)
library(network)
library(RSiena)
library(RsienaTwoStep)
library(igraph)
library(devtools)
```

## Data preparation for RSiena

Load data

```{r}
rm(list = ls())
load("./data/IndividualCharacteristics.RData")
load("./data/NetworkCharacteristics.RData")
load("./data/CivicAttitudes.RData")
```

<br>

Create network matrices

```{r}
# view(hanging[[1]])
hanging_df_t1 <- as.data.frame(hanging[[1]][1])
class(hanging_df_t1)
# view(hanging_df_t1)
strong_netw_t1 <- data.matrix(hanging_df_t1)
strong_netw_t1[strong_netw_t1==9]<-NA
class(strong_netw_t1)
# view(strong_netw_t1)

hanging_df_t2 <- as.data.frame(hanging[[1]][2])
class(hanging_df_t2)
# view(hanging_df_t2)
strong_netw_t2 <- data.matrix(hanging_df_t2)
strong_netw_t2[strong_netw_t2==9]<-NA
class(strong_netw_t2)
# view(strong_netw_t2)
```

<br>

Make civic attitudes scale

```{r}
#Wave 1
IC_df <- as.data.frame(T1civeng[[1]])
IC_df$missings <- rowSums(is.na(IC_df))
IC_df$ce_t1 <- ifelse(IC_df$missings <= 1, rowMeans(IC_df[,1:4]), NA)

#Wave 2
IC_df2 <- as.data.frame(T2civeng[[1]])
IC_df2$missings <- rowSums(is.na(IC_df2))
IC_df2$ce_t2 <- ifelse(IC_df2$missings <= 1, rowMeans(IC_df2[,1:4]), NA)
```

<br>

Putting the behavioural data in a matrix

```{r}
IC_df <- IC_df %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "id") 

IC_df2 <- IC_df2 %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "id") 

IC_df <- left_join(IC_df, IC_df2, by=c("id"))

behy <- IC_df %>% 
  dplyr::select("ce_t1", "ce_t2") %>% 
  as.matrix()
```

<br>

Creating an RSiena data frame

```{r}
behy <- sienaDependent(behy, type = c("behavior"))
nety <- sienaDependent(array(data= c(strong_netw_t1, strong_netw_t2), dim=c(dim(strong_netw_t1),2)))

mydata <- sienaDataCreate(behy, nety)
```

<br>

## Simplest model of RSiena

Run a model with no effects

```{r, eval=FALSE}
myAlgorithm <- sienaAlgorithmCreate(projname = "test")
myeff <- getEffects(mydata)
simple_model <- siena07(myAlgorithm, data = mydata, effects = myeff, returnDeps = TRUE)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# saveRDS(simple_model, "simple_model.rds")
simple_model <- readRDS("simple_model.rds")
```

```{r}
simple_model
```

<br>

### Interpretation

- Rate basic rate parameter nety:

  - **Question:** How do you intepret this?

- Eval outdegree (density):

  - Indicates how dense the network is.

  - In this case: A negative value, meaning that the chance of observing a tie is lower than the chance of not forming a tie

  - Nodes, in general, form relatively few ties (**question:** Relative to whom?)

- Eval reciprocity:

  - Indicated how often a tie that is formed is reciprocated

  - In this case: A positive value, meaning that the chance of observing a reciprocated tie is higher than the chance of not forming a reciprocated tie

  - Nodes, in general, prefer to form/ maintain ties to create a reciprocated relation, than start a relationship with a new person

- Rate rate behy period 1:

  - **Question:** How do you interpret this?

- Eval behy linear shape:

  - About how nodes who differ from the mean tend to change their behaviour (in this case assumed to be linear) **(Question?**)

- Eval behy quadratic shape:

  - About how nodes who differ from the mean tend to change their behaviour (in this case assumed to be quadratic) (**Question?**)

<br>

## Adding effects

Expected homophily effect of gender

```{r}
# Create gender variable
gender1 <- gender[[1]][,1]
gender2 <- gender[[1]][,2]
gender <- coalesce(gender1, gender2)
head(gender)

# Add gender as constant covariate
gender_covar <- coCovar(gender)
mydata_1 <- sienaDataCreate(nety, gender_covar, behy)
myeff_1 <- getEffects(mydata_1)

myeff_1 <- includeEffects(myeff_1, simX, interaction1 = "gender_covar")
```

Add effects for selection and influence for civic attitudes

```{r}
# General effects
myeff_1 <- includeEffects(myeff_1, egoX, altX, simX, interaction1 = "behy")

# Adding influence effects for indegree, outdegree and assimilation
myeff_1 <- includeEffects(myeff_1, name = "behy", avAlt, indeg, outdeg, interaction1 = "nety")

# Set algorithm
myCoEvAlgorithm <- sienaAlgorithmCreate(projname = "test")
```

Running the model

```{r, eval=FALSE}
model_week7 <- siena07(myCoEvAlgorithm, data = mydata_1, effects = myeff_1)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# saveRDS(model_week7, "model_week7.rds")
model_week7 <- readRDS("model_week7.rds")
```

```{r}
model_week7

# All convergence t-ratio should be <.1 --> is met
# Overall max convergence ratio should be <.25 --> is met (ratio = 0.1670)
```

<br>

### Interpretation

Network dynamics:

- Rate basic rate parameter nety:

  - **Question:** How do you intepret this?

- Eval outdegree (density):

  - Indicates how dense the network is.

  - In this case: A negative value, meaning that the chance of observing a tie is lower than the chance of not forming a tie

  - Nodes, in general, form relatively few ties (**question:** Relative to whom?)

- Eval reciprocity:

  - Indicated how often a tie that is formed is reciprocated

  - In this case: A positive value, meaning that the chance of observing a reciprocated tie is higher than the chance of not forming a reciprocated tie

  - Nodes, in general, prefer to form/ maintain ties to create a reciprocated relation, than start a relationship with a new person

- Eval gender_covar similarity:

  - How similar are connected ties with regards to the covar (in this case gender)

  - In this case: A positive value, meaning that it is more likely that *i* makes a tie with *j* compared to with *h* if *j* has the same gender as *i* (and *h* hasn't)

- Eval behy alter

  - About network homophily

  - Sender homophily --\> Does *i* prefer to send ties to someone similar to themselves

  - In this case: Negative value --\> *i* prefers to send a tie to alter *j* over alter *h*, where *j* has dissimilar preferences

- Eval behy ego

  - About network homophily

  - Receiver homophily --\> Does *i* get more ties from people with similar attitudes?

  - In this case: Negative value --\> *i* is more likely to get a tie from *j* than from *h*, where *j* has dissimilar preferences

- Eval behy similarity

  - About network homophily

<br>

Behaviour dynamics:

- Rate rate behy period 1:

  - **Question:** How do you interpret this?

- Eval behy linear shape:

  - About how nodes who differ from the mean tend to change their behaviour (in this case assumed to be linear) (**Question?**)

- Eval behy quadratic shape:

  - About how nodes who differ from the mean tend to change their behaviour (in this case assumed to be quadratic) (**Question?**)

  - The attractiveness of further steps up the behaviour ladder (this is the mountain I think), depends on where the actor is on the ladder

- Eval behy indegree:

  - Indegree tie is more likely when you have similar civic attitudes (positive value)

- Eval behy outdegree:

  - Outdegree tie is less likely when you have similar civic attitudes (negative value)

- Eval behy average alter:

  - About influence effects

  - Average alter effect --\> *i* behaviour multiplied by the average behaviour of their alters

  - In this case: A negative value --\> being friends with people with positive civic attitude scores, makes you more negative (?? huh?)
  
  - But it is not significant, so no effect

# In class
## Step 1: Base model
```{r}
gender_covar <- coCovar(gender)
mydata_1 <- sienaDataCreate(nety, gender_covar, behy)
myeff_2 <- getEffects(mydata_1)

# Start with a covariate for gender, with same-ego, same-alter, and same-x

myeff_2 <- includeEffects(myeff_2, egoX, altX, sameX, interaction1 = "gender_covar")

# Behavioural effects: egoX, AltX, and absDiffX
myeff_2 <- includeEffects(myeff_2, egoX, altX, absDiffX, interaction1 = "behy")

# Adding influence effects for indegree, outdegree and assimilation
# AvAlt_CC because that one updates its mean everytime, rather than using the grand mean
myeff_2 <- includeEffects(myeff_2, name = "behy", avAlt_CC, indeg, outdeg, interaction1 = "nety")

# maxAlt

# Set algorithm
myCoEvAlgorithm <- sienaAlgorithmCreate(projname = "test", MaxDegree = c(nety = 10))
```

Running the model
```{r, eval=FALSE}
model_week7_2 <- siena07(myCoEvAlgorithm, data = mydata_1, effects = myeff_2, returnDeps = TRUE)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# saveRDS(model_week7_2, "model_week7_2.rds")
model_week7_2 <- readRDS("model_week7_2.rds")
```

```{r}
model_week7_2

options(scipen = 50)

results <- data.frame(
  effect = model_week7_2$effects$effectName,
  b = model_week7_2$theta,
  se = model_week7_2$se,
  t = model_week7_2$theta / model_week7_2$se,
  p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(model_week7_2$theta / model_week7_2$se)))

results
```

## Goodness of fit
```{r}
gofi0 <- RSiena::sienaGOF(model_week7_4, IndegreeDistribution, verbose = FALSE, join = TRUE, varName = "nety")

gofo0 <- RSiena:: sienaGOF(model_week7_4, OutdegreeDistribution, verbose = FALSE, join = TRUE, levls = c(0:10, 15, 20), varName = "nety")

GeodesicDistribution <- function (i, data, sims, period, groupName,
  varName, levls=c(1:5,Inf), cumulative=TRUE, ...) {
  x <- networkExtraction(i, data, sims, period, groupName, varName)
  require(network)
  require(sna)
  a <- sna::geodist(symmetrize(x))$gdist
  if (cumulative)
  {
    gdi <- sapply(levls, function(i){ sum(a<=i) })
  }
  else
  {
    gdi <- sapply(levls, function(i){ sum(a==i) })
  }
  names(gdi) <- as.character(levls)
  gdi
}

gof0.gd <- RSiena:: sienaGOF(model_week7_4, GeodesicDistribution, cumulative = FALSE, verbose = FALSE, join = TRUE, varName = "nety")
```

```{r}
plot(gofi0)
plot(gofo0)
plot(gof0.gd)
```

Custum functions
```{r, eval = FALSE}
fsave <- function(x, file, location = "./data/processed/", ...) {
    if (!dir.exists(location))
        dir.create(location)
    datename <- substr(gsub("[:-]", "", Sys.time()), 1, 8)
    totalname <- paste(location, datename, file, sep = "")
    print(paste("SAVED: ", totalname, sep = ""))
    save(x, file = totalname)
}

fpackage.check <- function(packages) {
    lapply(packages, FUN = function(x) {
        if (!require(x, character.only = TRUE)) {
            install.packages(x, dependencies = TRUE)
            library(x, character.only = TRUE)
        }
    })
}

colorize <- function(x, color) {
    sprintf("<span style='color: %s;'>%s</span>", color, x)
}

fshowdf <- function(x, ...) {
    knitr::kable(x, digits = 3, "html", ...) %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) %>%
        kableExtra::scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "600px")
}

ts_rsienanets <- function(model_5) {
   n <- dim(model_5$f$Data1$depvars[[1]][, , 1])[1]
   sims <- foreach(i = 1:length(model_5$sims)) %dopar% {
     edges <- model_5$sims[[i]][[1]][[1]][[1]]
     # create empty adjacency matrix
     adj <- matrix(0, n, n)
     # put edge values in desired places
     adj[edges[, 1:2]] <- edges[, 3]
     adj
   }
   return(sims)
 }
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
packages = c("RsienaTwoStep", "RSiena", "ggplot2", "tidyverse", "kableExtra")

fpackage.check(packages)
```
